title: 7 Best HeyIris (Iris AI) Alternatives and Competitors in 2026
summary: Compare 7 HeyIris (Iris AI) alternatives by use case, from Inventive AI to Loopio and Responsive, with pricing, limitations, and ratings.
body_markdown:
Iris AI, sold at heyiris.ai and still searched as HeyIris, is AI RFP software priced per active user. Each seat includes unlimited RFPs, proposals, DDQs, and security questionnaires, and reviewers rate it 4.9/5 on G2 for fast drafts, cited answers, and responsive support.


Teams start looking at alternatives for a few specific reasons: the bill grows with every person who drafts, reviews, or approves, the price isn't published, and contradictions between sources still get caught in review. This guide compares seven alternatives by use case, with pricing and limitations for each, so you can match one to how your team works.


**TL;DR**


- Iris AI charges per active user and doesn't publish a price, so most teams switch over seat cost or content control.
- For many contributors at a flat cost plus conflict detection across sources, Inventive AI starts at $830/month with unlimited users.
- Pick Responsive for formal approvals, Loopio for a structured library, AutoRFP.ai for published project pricing, Arphie for questionnaires and DDQs, 1up for quick answers in Slack, and Ombud for branded templates.
- Iris still fits a small, high-volume team with a few power users.


## **Why do teams look for HeyIris alternatives?**


Most teams switch over cost structure or content control, not because Iris drafts poorly. The common reasons:


- **Per-seat cost climbs with contributors:** Iris charges for every active user who drafts, reviews, or approves, so pulling in SMEs from security, legal, and product raises the bill.
- **No published price:** you need a sales call for any number, which makes early budgeting harder.
- **Aging flags, not conflict checks:** Iris flags aging or expiring content, but two sources that contradict each other still get caught in review.
- **Output depends on your documentation:** reviewers say drafts can read robotic and need tone editing when source content is thin.
- **Speed on large files:** some reviewers report slow processing on long or complex documents.

## **1. Best HeyIris alternative for unlimited users and conflict detection: Inventive AI**


[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) suits teams that pull many contributors into each response and want cost to stay flat as the team grows. It drafts RFPs, DDQs, security questionnaires, and narrative proposals from your connected sources, with a citation and confidence score on every answer.


### **Inventive AI best features**


- **Connected knowledge:** Drafts from SharePoint, Google Drive, Confluence, Notion, Salesforce, and Zendesk instead of a hand-maintained Q&A library.
- **Conflict detection:** The Content Governance Agent flags outdated or contradicting content across sources before a response goes out.
- **Citations and confidence scores:** Every answer shows its source and how confident the AI is, and gaps are flagged rather than guessed.
- **Narrative and value sections:** Handles long-form value statements and executive summaries, not just short factual answers.
- **Agents beyond drafting:** Go/No-Go scoring, competitive intelligence, and project management for assignments and reviews.


### **Inventive AI limitations**


- Reporting dashboards offer less customization than some enterprise platforms.
- No native Jira integration yet.
- A newer platform with a smaller review base than Loopio or Responsive.


**Pricing:** Usage-based,[starting at $830/month, billed annually](https://www.inventive.ai/inventive-ai-pricing) , with unlimited users, and unused RFPs roll over.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.9/5](https://www.g2.com/products/inventive-ai/reviews) , Gartner Peer Insights[5/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/inventive-ai/product/inventive)


## **2. Best HeyIris alternative for enterprise governance and approvals: Responsive**


[Responsive](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/responsive-ai-rfpio-pricing-features-reviews) , formerly RFPIO, fits large teams where formal approval workflows and audit trails matter more than drafting speed. It's a library-based response platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, DDQs, and proposals. **‍**


### **Responsive best features**


- **AI drafting with scoring:** Drafts from the library with source citations, and TRACE Score rates each AI answer from 0 to 100.
- **Integrations:** About 30 native integrations and 75+ APIs across CRM, cloud storage, and collaboration tools.
- **Guest access:** Unlimited guest users, so occasional reviewers don't need a full license.
- **Hosting options:** Flexible hosting, including GovCloud, for regulated buyers.


### **Responsive limitations**


- The library still needs a content owner to stay accurate.
- A feature-dense interface with a steep learning curve for new users.
- Add-ons such as LookUp, translation, and premium connectors raise the total cost.


**Pricing:** The Emerging Edition starts from $10,000, and Vendr's data puts the median contract at $14,750 a year.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.5/5](https://www.g2.com/products/responsive-formerly-rfpio/reviews) , Gartner Peer Insights[4.3/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/responsive/product/responsive)


### **3. Best HeyIris alternative for a structured content library: Loopio**


[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) suits teams that answer repetitive, structured RFPs and want a well-organized library with clear workflows. It's a response management platform built around reusing approved answers.


### **Loopio best features**


- **Structured library:** Answers organized into stacks, categories, and tags, with duplicate detection and review cycles.
- **Answer suggestions:** Surfaces the best-matching approved answer for each question and drafts from the library.
- **Assignments and deadlines:** Routes questions to SMEs and tracks progress across projects.
- **Portals and AI assistants:** A browser extension for procurement portals, plus an MCP connection to Claude and ChatGPT.


### **Loopio limitations**


- AI drafts from the library, so answers go stale without a content owner.
- Seat-based pricing gets expensive as contributors are added.
- Reviewers report formatting fixes when exporting long projects.


**Pricing:** Quote-based. Vendr's data puts the median contract at $24,318 a year.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.6/5](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews) **,** Gartner Peer Insights:[4.4/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/loopio/product/loopio)


## 4. Best HeyIris alternative for published, project-based pricing: AutoRFP.ai


[AutoRFP.ai](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/autorfp-ai-pricing-features-reviews) fits teams with steady RFP volume that want a public price and unlimited users. It's an AI-native platform that drafts from your library, uploaded documents, and connected tools, with a Trust Score on each answer.


### AutoRFP.ai best features


- **Published pricing:** Two public plans with unlimited users and every feature included.
- **Trust Scores and sources:** Each draft shows its source and a confidence score, so reviewers check only what looks uncertain.
- **Portal Agent:** Drafts answers inside procurement and security portals from a Chrome side panel.
- **Free proof of concept:** A two-week trial on your own content before you sign.


### AutoRFP.ai limitations


- Pricing jumps between project tiers, and unused projects don't roll over.
- Reviewers note a learning curve in the interface.
- Questions in free-text PDFs need more manual cleanup.


**Pricing:** Scale is $899/month for 24 projects a year, and Accelerate is $1,299/month for 50, both billed yearly.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.9/5](https://www.g2.com/products/autorfp-ai/reviews) , Gartner Peer Insights[4.9/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/rfp-response-management-applications/vendor/autorfp-ai/product/autorfp-ai)


## **5. Best HeyIris alternative for questionnaires and DDQs: Arphie**


[Arphie](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/arphie-pricing-features-reviews) suits security and solutions teams whose volume is mostly questionnaires and DDQs. It's AI-native, connects to live sources, and shows a confidence score and source links on each draft.


### Arphie best features


- **Live sources:** Connects to where your information already lives, so there's no Q&A library to build first.
- **Confidence and sources:** Each draft shows a confidence score and the documents it drew from.
- **Content hygiene:** Merges duplicates and flags outdated answers for review.
- **Unlimited users:** Pricing is based on projects, not seats.


### Arphie limitations


- Analytics are narrow for leadership reporting.
- A newer platform with a small review base.
- Overage terms for going past your project allowance aren't published.


**Pricing:** Quote-based and priced by concurrent projects. Arphie's own pricing guide puts it at $36,000 to $60,000+ a year.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.9/5](https://www.g2.com/products/arphie/reviews) , from a small review base


## 6. Best HeyIris alternative for lightweight answers in Slack and the browser: 1up


1up fits smaller teams that want quick answers inside the tools they already use, more than a full RFP workflow. It drafts answers from your website, docs, and knowledge bases.


### 1up best features


- **Answers where you work:** Responds inside Slack, Microsoft Teams, and a browser extension for web-based questionnaires.
- **Broad use:** Covers internal sales questions and enablement as well as RFPs.
- **Low entry cost:** A free plan and paid plans from $300 a month.


### 1up limitations


- Lighter project management for long, multi-section RFPs.
- Answers can read generic on complex, deal-specific questions.
- Fewer approval and governance controls than enterprise platforms.


**Pricing:** Free plan; Starter $300/month; Plus $900/month; Enterprise custom.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.9/5](https://www.g2.com/products/1up/reviews)


## 7. Best HeyIris alternative for collaborative, template-based publishing: Ombud


Ombud suits teams where sales, legal, and security all contribute to responses and final documents must follow branded templates. It's a response platform for RFPs, security questionnaires, proposals, and SOWs.


### Ombud best features


- **Cross-functional collaboration:** Sales, legal, finance, and security contribute and review in one place.
- **Content approvals:** Approved answers stay centralized, which keeps responses consistent.
- **Branded publishing:** Exports to branded templates for proposals and SOWs.
- **Workflow tracking:** Assignments and deadlines across submissions.


### Ombud limitations


- Suggestions lean on rules and approved content more than generative drafting.
- Complex, open-ended questions need more manual work.
- Pricing isn't published.


**Pricing:** Custom quote.


**Ratings:**[G2 4.7/5](https://www.g2.com/products/ombud/reviews)

## When is Iris still the right choice?


Iris is still a strong fit for a small, dedicated RFP or security team that handles high volume with a few power users. In that setup, per-seat pricing with unlimited usage stays predictable, and Iris's cited answers and responsive support are what reviewers rate highest. Before you switch, count who would actually need a seat:[HeyIris pricing](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/heyiris-ai-pricing-features-reviews) stays predictable when that number is small.


## Why choose Inventive AI over other HeyIris alternatives?


Choose Inventive AI if many people contribute to each response and you want contradictions between sources caught before review. Most tools on this list speed up drafting or reuse approved answers. Inventive also checks that what it drafts is current and consistent across your sources.


Inventive AI fits teams that need:


- **Answers that reflect the deal:** Drafts draw on the buyer's requirements and your connected sources, so responses fit the opportunity in front of you.
- **Accuracy on long, complex RFPs:** Every answer carries a citation and a confidence score, and gaps go to an SME instead of getting a guessed answer.
- **Safer security and compliance sections:** The Content Governance Agent flags outdated or conflicting content before it reaches a reviewer.
- **Strong narrative sections:** Value statements and executive summaries draft from the same sources as short factual answers.
- **Flat cost as the team grows:** Unlimited users on every plan, so pulling in SMEs doesn't raise the bill.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is HeyIris the same as Iris AI?


Yes. Iris is the product, sold at heyiris.ai, and many buyers still search for it as HeyIris. Everything on this page applies to both names.


### How much does Iris AI cost?


Iris doesn't publish a price. It charges per active user, meaning anyone who drafts, reviews, or approves responses, on annual or multi-year contracts, and seats added mid-term are prorated.


### Is Iris suitable for enterprise RFP teams?


It can be. Iris includes SSO, SAML, SCIM, and a dedicated customer success manager, and reports 300+ customers. It works best when the number of people who need a paid seat stays manageable.


### Which HeyIris alternative is the cheapest?


1up has a free plan and paid plans from $300 a month. Among full RFP platforms with public prices, Inventive AI starts at $830 a month and AutoRFP.ai at $899, both with unlimited users.


### Does Iris offer a free trial?


Not a self-serve one. Iris offers a guided evaluation and proof of concept, and its free RFP analyzer lets you test go/no-go scoring on a past RFP.


### HeyIris vs 1up: which is better?


Iris is the fuller RFP platform, with project workflows and cited drafting priced per seat. 1up is lighter and cheaper, and suits teams that mostly want quick answers inside Slack or a browser.


### Can I move my Iris content to another tool?


Usually, yes. Most platforms import past responses and approved answers, and AI-native tools can also connect to your source documents directly. Confirm export options in your Iris contract before you switch.
